questions.text: "I think electric vehicles ___ dominate the market by 2035." (opinion prediction)
questions.hint: "I think / believe" + prediction = will

questions.text: "The battery is almost empty — the drone ___ fall." (visible evidence)
questions.hint: Evidence-based immediate prediction = going to

questions.text: "When AI ___ (become) more capable, governments ___ (need) new laws."
questions.hint: Time clause: present simple; result: will + infinitive

questions.text: "We ___ with the development team on Thursday." (arranged, in the calendar)
questions.hint: Fixed future arrangement = present continuous

questions.text: "By 2040, researchers ___ a viable quantum computer." Choose the correct form.
questions.hint: "By + future time" = future perfect: will have + pp

questions.text: "In 2035, most white-collar workers ___ (collaborate) with AI tools daily." (ongoing activity)
questions.hint: Future continuous: typical ongoing activity at a future time

questions.text: "AI ___ transform medicine — it's already happening in diagnostics." (evidence-based, formal)
questions.hint: "is expected to" = formal evidence-based prediction

questions.text: "By next year, she ___ (work) on AI safety research for five years." (duration until future)
questions.hint: Future perfect continuous: will have been + -ing

questions.text: "The new law is ___ come into effect in March." (scheduled, formal)
questions.hint: "is due to" = scheduled to happen at a specific time

questions.text: "When AI ___ mature, it will reshape the economy." — What is WRONG here?
opts: "Will mature" should be "matures" in a time clause
questions.correct: "Will mature" should be "matures" in a time clause
questions.hint: Time clauses use present simple, not will

questions.text: What does "the digital divide" refer to?
opts: The gap between old and new technology
The gap between those with and without digital access
The difference between AI and human intelligence
The divide between digital and physical workplaces
questions.correct: The gap between those with and without digital access
questions.hint: Reading 1: "digital divide"

questions.text: "Technology ___ (likely / disrupt) traditional industries significantly over the next decade."
questions.hint: "is likely to + infinitive"

questions.text: Which is the most academic way to predict AI's future impact?
opts: AI is going to change everything soon.
I think AI will help a lot.
AI is predicted to transform multiple sectors within the next decade.
AI is about to make big changes.
questions.correct: AI is predicted to transform multiple sectors within the next decade.
questions.hint: "is predicted to + infinitive" = formal, evidence-based, academic

questions.text: "Unless governments invest in retraining, many workers will be left behind" — this conditional is correct.
questions.hint: "Unless" = if not; present simple in condition, will in result

questions.text: What does Amara's Law say?
opts: Technology always develops exactly as predicted
We overestimate short-term impact and underestimate long-term impact
AI will inevitably replace all human jobs
Predictions about technology are always wrong
questions.correct: We overestimate short-term impact and underestimate long-term impact
questions.hint: Listening 3B: Prof. Seitkali quotes Amara's Law

questions.text: "The seminar ___ at 10am." (official timetable — present simple)
questions.hint: Fixed timetable: present simple

questions.text: "As soon as the results ___ (publish), we ___ (analyse) them."
questions.hint: Time clause: present simple (passive); result: will

questions.text: "___ you ___ using the lab tomorrow?" (Polite future enquiry)
questions.hint: Polite enquiry: Will you be + -ing?

questions.text: What does the text say about workers who "lack access to education or retraining"?
opts: They will benefit most from AI
They are most likely to retrain successfully
They are encouraged to start businesses
questions.hint: Reading 1: "find themselves left behind"

questions.text: "By the time the AI regulations pass, much of the damage ___ (do)." (passive future perfect)
questions.hint: Future perfect passive: will have been + pp

questions.text: Which uses "be about to" correctly?
opts: The company is about to launching its product.
The company is about launch its product.
The company is about to launch its product.
The company about to launch its product.
questions.correct: The company is about to launch its product.
questions.hint: "is about to + bare infinitive"

questions.text: The replacement of human labour by machines is called ___.
questions.hint: Reading 1: "automation — replacement of human labour by machines"

questions.text: "I've already decided — I ___ study machine learning next year." (pre-made intention)
questions.hint: Pre-made intention = going to

questions.text: "Technology is likely transforming education" is grammatically correct.
questions.hint: "is likely to transform" — must use "to + infinitive" after "likely"

questions.text: To "augment" human capabilities means to…
opts: Add to them, making them greater
questions.correct: Add to them, making them greater
questions.hint: Reading 2: "augment human capabilities"
